contexts.text: He shall trample on thy head ()... To trample on = depression. AC 258.
When the goods and truths of faith are perverted by natural lumen, it is described by the feet and hoofs of a beast... by which foods are trampled on. Illustrated.
To tread, and trample, in anger () = victories over evils... To trample, in the Word, is predicated of evil. TCR 116. AE 922:5.
To tread down the streets () = to destroy the Knowledges of truth.
Since they disperse the truths still remaining and scattered... it is said that they trample on the pieces of silver ().
To trample on = to cast down.

The holy city they shall trample on forty-two months () = that it had dispersed all the truth of the Word until not any remains. ( = that they will destroy all the doctrine of good and truth from the Word, AE 632.)
A nation trodden down () = those outside the Church... AE 331:5.
They have trodden down My field () = the vastation of the Church.
To trample on... = to destroy, which is done by those who are natural and sensuous...
To trample down = to completely destroy.

Moreover, in the Spiritual World, those who deny and despise the truths of Heaven and the Church appear to trample them with the soles of their feet; and this because the external Sensuous of man corresponds to the soles... To trample is predicated of such in the following passages. Fully illustrated.
A carcase trodden on () = an infernal Spirit with whom everything is spiritually dead from the complete destruction of good.
Jerusalem shall be trampled down () = the complete destruction and perversion of the doctrine of the Church.
Lest they trample on them with their feet () = to wholly reject as filth.
